title: Verify and source the caramelization temperature claims in the kitchen-chemistry learning path (sugar melting/onset thresholds)
question: What are the scientifically correct melting points and caramelization onset temperatures for fructose, glucose, sucrose and maltose, and is the hard-threshold framing of the KARAMELL path ('Zucker beginnt bei etwa 160°C zu schmelzen', 'Unter 160°C passiert nichts', 'Fruchtzucker 110 / Traubenzucker 150 / Haushaltszucker 160 / Malzzucker 180 Grad') accurate, or is caramelization a temperature- and time-dependent rate process with sucrose actually melting near 186°C?
why_now: The prototype path PATH:SSF:CHE-KUECHE-KARAMELL-0001 (registered in lib/learningPathRegistry.ts and linked as an optional branch from the Maillard path) teaches exact sugar thresholds as crisp facts to NOXIA learners. Sucrose melts at about 186°C with simultaneous decomposition and caramelization is a rate process, so the current claims likely mis-teach phase behaviour. A sourced correction before the path ships protects educational quality and the KG chemistry entities (CON:CHE-ORGANIC, KD:CHE-THERMAL) it feeds.
real_world_anchor: Melting points and caramelization onset temperatures of fructose, glucose, sucrose and maltose; whether a hard 160°C onset threshold is scientifically accurate
